answer: Each agent can earn only one nontransferable identity credential by completing a randomized, costly task that requires sustained participation, while independent validators check the result before issuing it. A lantern beacon might reveal task assignments just in time; a haven preserves completed work if a validator drops out, and a nebula of validators makes collusion harder. To multiply identities, an attacker must pay the task cost repeatedly and keep each identity active, rather than cheaply minting accounts.
